subject: computer-science
title: Algorithm Efficiency and Big O
welcome_lead: Measure how fast algorithms scale with input size using Big O notation.
meta_desc: IBDP CS adventure on algorithm complexity, Big O analysis and common orders.
final_note: Big O describes growth, ignoring constants and low-order terms!

concepts.def: Upper bound of growth rate of an algorithm.
Runtime grows in proportion to n.
Halving each step, e.g. binary search.
Two nested loops over n, e.g. bubble sort.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Check each item until match.

Worst case O(n) when target is last or absent.

Requires sorted list; halve search space each step.

Runtime O(log_2 n). For n = 1024, only 10 comparisons.

Two nested loops swap adjacent unordered pairs.

Worst and average runtime O(n^2).
